author: agent-3
exposureWarning: This artifact is DOWNSTREAM of two contested decisions — the fact plane (C-1, sealed but re-derived twice) and the plan/stage model (C-2, currently CANDIDATE after a v1 rejection). If the clean-sheet comparison overturns either, this artifact is redone. It was deliberately held back for that reason and is authored now only because the coordinator asked for completion.
purpose: Decide the two spine-exposed items: body-hash normalisation policy, and the imperative escape hatch's contract and budget model.

decisionDependencies.claim: no global tier ordering; rules declare requirements
typed logical stages; physical materialisation private; requiredness explicit
body-hash normalisation is the hardest decision to change later because baselines depend on it
fingerprint recipe is host-owned and versioned independently of the fact schema
user-custody changes need migrators and dual-emit windows
finding channel bandwidth is a resource to budget

bodyHashNormalisation.whyThisIsHard: Body hashes power duplicate detection, and duplicate findings get baselined. A normalisation change therefore re-identifies findings across every user's committed baseline — the user-custody hazard. It is a one-way door in the sense that widening later is cheap and narrowing later is not.

decision.form: A LADDER of named, independently versioned normalisation levels, not one policy.
decision.why: A single policy forces one tradeoff on every consumer. Exact-duplicate detection and near-duplicate detection want different normalisation, and forcing one loses either precision or recall permanently.

levels.normalises: nothing — raw bytes of the body span
levels.stability: maximally stable; changes only when the file changes

levels.rationale: Formatting churn is not duplication. Excluding it is the minimum that makes the feature useful, and it is the least contestable normalisation.
Two bodies differing only in comments are usually genuine duplication — but sometimes the comment is the difference. Opt-in because the judgment is contextual.

levels.normalises: L2 plus consistent renaming of local identifiers
levels.rationale: This finds copy-paste-and-rename, the highest-value duplication class. It also produces the most false positives, so it must never be a default.

rules.rule: Each level is separately versioned. A change to L2's comment grammar does not touch L1 identities, so it does not disturb baselines that only used L1.
The level and its version are part of the fact's identity and enter the derivation key. Two levels are two facts, never one fact computed differently.
A finding records the level that produced it. A baseline entry therefore pins a level, and comparing across levels is a typed mismatch rather than a silent diff.
Level normalisation is language-aware — comment and identifier syntax differ per language — but the LEVEL SEMANTICS are language-independent, so a rule can require L2 without knowing the language.
Changing an existing level's algorithm is a user-custody breaking change: migrator plus dual-emit window. Adding a NEW level is additive and free.
Never normalise away anything a rule might need to report. The finding must be able to show the actual source, so the L0 span is always retained alongside whatever level matched.

decision.escapeFromTheOneWayDoor: The ladder is what makes this reversible. Because adding a level is additive (BH-5) and levels are separately versioned (BH-1), a wrong default can be corrected by adding a level and migrating the default — not by redefining an existing identity. That converts an irreversible decision into a reversible one, which is the only reason this artifact is willing to decide it while the spine is contested.

imperativeEscapeHatch.purpose: Rules whose predicate cannot be expressed in the declarative IR. Not rules that need type information — those declare a fact-quality requirement (C-1) and remain declarative.
whenItIsTheRightTool: predicates over aggregates the IR cannot express
iteration whose bound depends on the data
whenItIsNotTheRightTool: needing resolved references — that is a declared requirement
needing type facts — that is a declared requirement
needing to read a file — that is never available at any tier

contract.input: A FactQuery handle scoped to the rule's DECLARED requirements. A query outside the declaration is a typed error, not a wider result.
contract.output: Findings with typed subjects and canonical proof anchors. The rule never computes a fingerprint — the host does, from the anchors.
contract.why_no_cross_rule: Rule-to-rule dependency would make evaluation order semantic, and order-dependence is how a concurrency change silently alters a verdict.

dimensions.why: bounds fan-out against the fact plane
the real cost driver; query count alone permits one unbounded query
TM.F3 — the finding channel is exfiltration bandwidth and a denial-of-merge vector

onExhaustion.requiredRule: Coverage entry plus policy indeterminate (c2 requiredness).
onExhaustion.rule: Exhaustion NEVER silently truncates findings. Truncation without a marker converts a budget into a correctness bug.

budgetModel.attribution: Exhaustion names the rule and, where determinable, the input that drove it (TM.F9).

determinism.requirement: An imperative rule declares itself deterministic or not. A non-deterministic rule cannot participate in a digest-equality claim, and its findings are marked accordingly.
determinism.enforcement: Absent clock, entropy, filesystem and cross-rule access (see `absent`), non-determinism is hard to reach — but declaring it is still required rather than inferred, because inference would be a guess.

imperativeEscapeHatch.tierPlacement: First-party imperative rules are linked TCB. Third-party imperative rules require the capability-scoped component tier — a signature does not confine anything (the sealed confinement-honesty limit).

conformanceTests.assert: Two normalisation levels over one body produce two distinct fact identities, both retained.
A finding records its normalisation level; comparing a baseline entry pinned to L1 against an L2 result is a typed mismatch, not a diff.
Adding a new level does not change any existing level's identities.
Changing an existing level's algorithm without a migrator and dual-emit window is refused by the release gate.
The L0 span is retrievable for any finding produced at any level (BH-6).
An imperative rule querying outside its declared requirements receives a typed error, not a wider result set.
An imperative rule has no reachable filesystem, network, spawn, clock, entropy, storage, or cross-rule access (closure-analysed, not asserted).
Exhausting any budget produces a Coverage entry; for a REQUIRED rule it forces indeterminate; findings are never silently truncated.
An imperative rule cannot compute or influence a fingerprint; identical anchors from different rules yield host-computed identities.
A rule declared non-deterministic is excluded from digest-equality claims and its findings are marked.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: fingerprints are host-computed from typed anchors
user-custody changes need migrators and dual-emit
required partial coverage cannot yield pass

peerReviewRequired: Is the ladder genuinely reversible, or does pinning a level into baselines create the same lock-in one level down? BH-5 claims additive levels are free; that claim deserves attack.
Is L1-lexical the right default, or is L2 defensible as default given how often comments differ trivially?
Is forbidding cross-rule results too strict? It rules out legitimate composition, at the cost of making order non-semantic.
rowsExamined as a budget assumes the fact plane can meter it. If it cannot, the budget is unenforceable and queryCount is all there is.
knownLimitations: SPINE-EXPOSED: downstream of C-1 and C-2. A clean-sheet divergence on fact representation or stage model invalidates this.
The ladder is a novel framing authored here and has had no adversarial review; its reversibility argument is the load-bearing claim and is untested.
Language-specific normalisation grammars are asserted to exist per level; none is specified.
rowsExamined metering may not be implementable depending on the storage engine, which is itself deferred.
